dedupe_keys.name: sigma plan integrated flood protection and controlled flood areas on the scheldt estuary belgium

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Sigma Plan, the flood protection plan for the Scheldt river and its tributaries (Rupel, Nete and Durme) in Flanders, Belgium, first adopted in 1977 after the 1976 storm surge flood. It protects about 20,000 hectares by combining dike reinforcement with controlled flood areas and, since the 2005 update, integrates flood protection with nature restoration under Natura 2000 and recreation. The 2005 update was based on a cost-benefit analysis of about 180 alternatives and took climate change and sea level rise projections into account; its cost was estimated at 882 million euro in 2005 and revised to about 994 million euro for works plus 62 million euro for accompanying measures in 2010. Projects are launched every five years, works under the 2005 plan run to 2030, and later work depends on the pace of sea level rise. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal. Caveats: figures are plan estimates, benefits are not quantified on the page, and the plan links to port expansion compensation. It illustrates long-term adaptation planning and investment appraisal of hybrid grey and green flood defences; a related record is the Global NbS opportunity areas dataset.
